diagnosis.root_cause: Two FreeRADIUS radcheck rows exist for the same username. The orphan row contains lineid 1C:EF:03:90:2B:5A instead of the subscriber's valid CRM lineid 00:A1:07:C4:1D:88, causing inconsistent session attribution and repeated authentication disconnects.
evidence: The customer has 19 sessions in 24 hours and 118 in seven days, well above the normal 2-3 sessions per day and within the session-flapping range.
Sessions are very short, with an average duration of 38 minutes versus the 11.9-hour network mean, indicating repeated service interruption or reauthentication.
RADIUS explicitly reports two rows for the same username, one valid and one orphaned, with conflicting lineids; FreeRADIUS may resolve either row first.
The customer is currently online and authenticated, so this is not a persistent ONU-offline condition.
RX power is normal at approximately -20.6 dBm, TX power is normal at approximately +2.45 dBm, and both optical values are stable over seven days.
Distance is constant at 96 km and TX bias current remains within the healthy range, ruling out distance change and meaningful laser degradation.
All sampled ONUs on EPON0/5 are online with normal optical readings, so there is no evidence of a PON-port or splitter fault.
The OLT, router, VLAN 1055, and live SNMP probes are healthy, ruling out OLT, router, VLAN, and general provisioning failures.
OLT population is 268 online of 281, consistent with the stated offline baseline and not indicative of an OLT-wide outage.

remediation.action: Remove the orphan radcheck row for username 30:16:9D:A2:5F:03, retain and verify the row containing lineid 00:A1:07:C4:1D:88, synchronize the corrected record to all RADIUS replicas, terminate stale sessions, and allow the customer to authenticate again. Monitor session count and duration afterward and audit the provisioning process for duplicate username/lineid creation.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two radcheck rows exist for the same username. FreeRADIUS resolves inconsistently between them, so authentication succeeds or fails depending on which row is matched, producing repeated short sessions and two alternating IP assignments.
expected_reasoning: 19 sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline, with a 38 minute mean duration against an 11.9 hour norm
RX has been flat at -20.6 dBm for seven days inside the +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so signal is not the cause
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable
Port neighbours are normal and the OLT is healthy, so no shared infrastructure fault
With no optical explanation available, the search moves to the authentication layer
RADIUS holds two radcheck rows for username 30:16:9D:A2:5F:03, one of them an orphan with a different lineid
Recent sessions alternate between two IP addresses, consistent with inconsistent row resolution
Traffic is erratic rather than declining, which fits intermittent authentication rather than a degrading link

expected_escalation.review_reason: Duplicate RADIUS rows must be resolved by hand; deleting the wrong row disconnects the customer

distractors: The session pattern is identical to signal-related flapping and invites that diagnosis
Zero-throughput windows in the speed series look like link loss but coincide with rejected auth
ONU is a Router type, inviting a CPE-fault explanation
